stem:
Meena's school has two water tanks on the roof. Tank P is tall and narrow, and the water level in it is 4.0 m above the ground-floor tap. Tank Q is short and wide, holds much more water in total, but the water level in it is only 2.5 m above an identical ground-floor tap.
Both taps are opened fully. Which statement about the water pressure at the taps is correct?

options.text: The tap from tank P has greater pressure, because the height of water above it is greater.
The tap from tank Q has greater pressure, because tank Q holds more water in total.
Both taps have equal pressure, because both tanks are on the same roof.
The tap from tank Q has greater pressure, because a wider tank pushes water out faster.

teacher.key_rationale: Liquid pressure at a point depends on the depth (height of liquid above the point) and the density of the liquid, not on the total volume of water or the width of the container. Tank P has the greater water height (4.0 m > 2.5 m) above its tap, so its tap has the greater pressure. Option A is correct.
